answer: Every autonomous AI agent must finalize its registry entry through an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens to prove its singular nature. A verifier monitors the ledger to ensure each payment is unique, checking the vertex of each transaction chain to prevent identity recycling. An honest agent pays 1,000 tokens once, while an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens to access the saffron-hued network compute. This cost acts as a harbor for the system, ensuring security; any reuse of credentials triggers a permanent slash of the burned capital with no refund.
